views.note: xml_loc=44: payment.provider form inheritance (payment_provider_views.xml: dpo_service_ref + dpo_company_token fields). QWeb redirect-form template in payment_dpo_templates.xml (auto-submit GET to payv2.php?ID={transaction_token}). No own model views.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._get_specific_rendering_values -> _dpo_create_token -> POST https://secure.3gdirectpay.com/API/v6/ (XML createToken) -> redirect to payv2.php?ID={token}
behavioral_notes.observation: _get_specific_rendering_values (payment_transaction.py) calls _dpo_create_token(), which builds an XML payload using Python f-strings: <API3G><CompanyToken>{dpo_company_token}</CompanyToken><Request>createToken</Request><Transaction> block with PaymentAmount, PaymentCurrency, CompanyRef=self.reference, RedirectURL and BackURL both pointing to /payment/dpo/return, customerEmail, customerFirstName (split via payment_utils.split_partner_name), customerLastName, customerCity, customerCountry (country code), customerZip </Transaction><Services><Service><ServiceType>{dpo_service_ref}</ServiceType><ServiceDescription>{reference}</ServiceDescription><ServiceDate>{create_date formatted %Y/%m/%d %H:%M}</ServiceDate></Service></Services></API3G>. It sends this via self._send_api_request('POST', '', data=payload) (the empty string endpoint is resolved by _build_request_url to the fixed API base). On success, it extracts transaction_data.get('TransToken') from the parsed XML response and returns {'api_url': f'https://secure.3gdirectpay.com/payv2.php?ID={transaction_token}'}. The QWeb redirect template auto-submits the browser to that URL. If _send_api_request raises ValidationError, _set_error is called and None is returned. The XML construction, the two-field credentials (service_ref + company_token), and the redirect-URL building are invisible to model/field metadata.

controllers/main.py DPOController._return_url='/payment/dpo/return' handles the GET redirect from the DPO hosted page. It calls _verify_and_process(data) where data is the GET query string. _verify_and_process first locates the transaction with payment.transaction.sudo()._search_by_reference('dpo', data) (which routes through _extract_reference -> data.get('CompanyRef')). It then POSTs a second XML request to the API with <Request>verifyToken</Request> and <TransactionToken>{data.get('TransID')}</TransactionToken>, merges the XML response dict into data via data.update(verified_data), and calls tx_sudo._process('dpo', data). The two-stage design (createToken on checkout start, verifyToken on return) means DPO's transaction state is never trusted from the redirect URL query string alone -- the return handler always re-validates against the DPO API before updating the Odoo transaction state. This server-side verify-before-process pattern and its ValidationError guard ('Unable to verify the payment data') are invisible to metadata.

payment_provider.py overrides three parent engine hooks to configure the DPO API channel: _build_request_url returns the fixed string 'https://secure.3gdirectpay.com/API/v6/' for every call (ignoring the endpoint argument entirely -- there is only one API endpoint), _build_request_headers returns {'Content-Type': 'application/xml; charset=utf-8'} (DPO uses XML, not JSON), and _parse_response_content parses response.content.decode('utf-8') via xml.etree.ElementTree.fromstring() and flattens all child elements into a plain dict {element.tag: element.text}. This means the parent engine's _send_api_request (which calls these hooks) transparently posts XML and returns a flat Python dict -- callers in payment_transaction.py work with this dict directly (e.g. transaction_data.get('TransToken'), payment_data.get('Result'), payment_data.get('TransID')). The XML wire format, the single-endpoint URL, and the stdlib ET parsing are invisible to model/field metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._apply_updates -- DPO Result code mapping to Odoo state machine via const.PAYMENT_STATUS_MAPPING
behavioral_notes.observation: _apply_updates (payment_transaction.py) sets self.provider_reference = payment_data.get('TransID') then dispatches on payment_data.get('Result') against const.PAYMENT_STATUS_MAPPING: pending=('003','007') -> _set_pending(); authorized=('001','005') or done=('000','002') -> _set_done() (both authorized and done collapse to done, no two-step capture implemented); cancel=('900'-'904','950') -> _set_canceled(); error=('801'-'804') -> _set_error() with a human-readable message built from ResultExplanation; any unknown code -> _set_error('Unknown status code'). _extract_amount_data extracts TransactionAmount (float) and TransactionCurrency (string) for the engine's amount cross-check. _extract_reference returns data.get('CompanyRef') to match the Odoo tx by reference. The full status-code table is defined in const.py with a pointer to https://docs.dpopay.com/api/index.html#tag/Basic-Transaction-Operations/operation/verifyToken. None of these status codes, the ResultExplanation field, or the authorized+done collapse are visible from metadata.

it_architecture.application: payment_dpo (DPO Group acquirer adapter for the payment engine; _inherit-only on provider/transaction; XML API createToken/verifyToken two-stage redirect flow)
software_services: /payment/dpo/return (http GET, auth=public: redirect-return from DPO hosted page; calls _verify_and_process -> verifyToken XML -> _process -> /payment/status)
data_objects: payment.transaction (DPO two-stage XML flow; no new fields; provider_reference=TransID)
logical_data_erm: payment.transaction -> payment.provider (provider_id; provider_code=='dpo' gates every override)
external: payment.transaction.reference == DPO XML CompanyRef (cross-system reference key for return-URL lookup)
external: payment.transaction.provider_reference == DPO TransID (set in _apply_updates from verifyToken response)
external: DPO TransToken (temporary session token: created by createToken, consumed by payv2.php redirect and verifyToken)
information_flows: outbound (createToken): _get_specific_rendering_values -> _dpo_create_token -> POST https://secure.3gdirectpay.com/API/v6/ (XML, Content-Type: application/xml; charset=utf-8, auth=dpo_company_token embedded in payload) -> parse XML response -> extract TransToken
outbound (browser redirect): QWeb template auto-submits GET to https://secure.3gdirectpay.com/payv2.php?ID={TransToken} -> DPO hosted payment page
outbound (verifyToken): _verify_and_process -> POST https://secure.3gdirectpay.com/API/v6/ (XML verifyToken with TransID) -> parse XML response -> data.update(verified_data)
inbound (process): merged data -> tx._process('dpo', data) -> _apply_updates -> state machine (_set_pending/_set_done/_set_canceled/_set_error based on Result code)
no client-side JS or SDK; no webhook/IPN (single redirect-return + server-side verify pattern)
frontend_components: QWeb redirect-form template (payment_dpo_templates.xml: auto-submit GET to payv2.php?ID={transaction_token}; no JS patches or OWL components)

external_integrations.sdk: none (no Python SDK; uses stdlib xml.etree.ElementTree for XML and payment engine's _send_api_request for HTTP)
endpoints: https://secure.3gdirectpay.com/API/v6/ (XML API: createToken and verifyToken operations)
external_integrations.auth: Company token embedded in XML request body (<CompanyToken>{dpo_company_token}</CompanyToken>); no HTTP auth headers
external_integrations.pattern: Two-stage XML redirect: (1) server-side createToken POST to API produces a TransToken; (2) browser is redirected to payv2.php?ID={TransToken} for hosted card entry; (3) on return, server immediately calls verifyToken POST to validate the outcome before updating the Odoo transaction state. The company token travels in the XML body, not in HTTP headers. Uses no webhook/IPN -- the single return-redirect plus server-side verify is the authoritative settlement path.

capabilities: Accept card and mobile-money payments across African markets via DPO Group hosted checkout (redirect flow)
Create a DPO transaction token server-side (createToken API) with full customer and service details embedded
Redirect payer to the DPO hosted payment page (payv2.php) with the transaction token
Verify the payment outcome server-side on return (verifyToken API) before updating Odoo transaction state
Map DPO Result codes to Odoo payment states (pending / done / canceled / error) with human-readable ResultExplanation on error
Restrict DPO company token to system administrators (base.group_system)
value_streams: Collect-Payment (redirect): _get_specific_rendering_values -> _dpo_create_token -> POST createToken XML -> TransToken -> browser redirect to payv2.php?ID={token} -> payer completes on DPO hosted page -> GET /payment/dpo/return -> _verify_and_process -> POST verifyToken XML -> _process('dpo', merged_data) -> _apply_updates -> _set_done/_set_canceled/_set_error -> redirect /payment/status
information_concepts: payment.transaction (DPO session: CompanyRef=reference for lookup, TransID=provider_reference, TransToken=ephemeral redirect key)
organization: (no module-owned res.groups; dpo_company_token restricted to base.group_system; everything else inherits payment's groups)
policies: Server-side verify-before-process: return route never trusts query-string parameters alone; always calls verifyToken API before calling _process, preventing replay or tampered-redirect attacks
Company token travels in XML body only (never in URL or HTTP headers); restricted to base.group_system field group
Authorized and Done DPO codes (001/005 and 000/002) both map to _set_done() -- no two-step capture; all charges are immediate settle
On createToken API error (ValidationError), tx is set to error state and no redirect token is produced
Unknown Result codes are logged as warnings and mapped to _set_error('Unknown status code')
stakeholders: Payer / Customer (res.partner; pays via DPO hosted page in supported African countries)
Merchant / Company (res.company; holds DPO Service ID and Company Token)
DPO Group (Direct Pay Online; African payment processor and acquirer network)
Accountant (consumes settled payments via account_payment downstream)
metrics: (no own reports; transaction volumes/amounts/states surfaced by the parent payment.transaction pivot/graph)

classification.apqc_category: 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (9.5 process payments / collect cash; manage external payment provider)
classification.rationale: payment_dpo is a value-NETWORK (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating-technology) component: a concrete acquirer adapter connecting payers in African markets to the merchant via the DPO Group payment network. It exhibits the canonical mediating-technology activities: network promotion/contract management (DPO Service ID and Company Token configuration), service provisioning (createToken + verifyToken per transaction), and infrastructure operation (the XML API link to secure.3gdirectpay.com and the hosted-redirect payment page). It inherits the parent 'payment' engine's network position exactly. activity_class='support': payment acceptance is a finance/infrastructure support function under APQC 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (category Accounting/Payment Providers, application=False).

standard_capabilities: hosted-redirect card and mobile-money payment acceptance via DPO Group across African markets
server-side createToken (XML) to obtain a session token before redirecting
server-side verifyToken (XML) on return to authenticate the outcome before state update
DPO Result code -> Odoo state mapping (pending/done/canceled/error) with ResultExplanation on error
typical_fits: e-commerce / portal checkout for customers in Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, Ghana, Uganda, and other DPO-covered African markets
invoice payment online via DPO hosted checkout (account_payment / sale downstream)
multi-currency African payment acceptance (DPO supports local currencies per market)
common_gaps: no tokenization / saved card support (no _extract_token_values override; DPO hosted page does not expose a re-usable card token to Odoo)
no in-module refund operation (no _send_refund_request override; refunds must be done via DPO dashboard)
no webhook/IPN path -- relies entirely on the redirect-return GET; if the customer closes the browser before the return redirect, the transaction stays in draft
no manual authorize-then-capture (authorized and done codes both collapse to _set_done()); immediate settlement only
no Express Checkout / wallet-pay support (redirect-only, no JS integration)
local/dev instances need a public URL for the /payment/dpo/return redirect to work

open_questions: What happens if the customer closes the browser before the return redirect fires -- is there any scheduled job or webhook fallback to settle the transaction?
Does DPO provide a test/sandbox environment with known CompanyToken and ServiceID values for automated testing?
The authorized Result codes (001/005) collapse to _set_done() -- does DPO actually send these codes in practice, and does the merchant need a separate capture step outside Odoo?
What African currencies and payment methods are supported at the payv2.php hosted page -- are they configurable from the Odoo provider settings or purely from the DPO merchant account?
